message.abstract: Carbon materials generated from biomass garner significant interest for supercapacitor applications owing to their elevated specific capacitance, affordability, environmental sustainability, and the availability of natural precursors. In this work, oxygen-rich porous carbons are fabricated using sodium thiosulfate (Na₂S₂O₃)—a less toxic activating agent compared to conventional chemicals. The structural and textural characteristics of the resulting carbons are strongly influenced by the synthesis parameters. Among the prepared samples, HTWB-0.5-900 exhibits a well-developed hierarchical network consisting of micro-, meso-, and macropores and possesses a high surface area of 1018.74 m²/g, features that enhance ion transport and increase the accessibility of electrocatalytically active sites. When applied as a supercapacitor electrode, the HTWB-0.5-900 material, obtained at 900°C using a Na₂S₂O₃/HTWB mass ratio of 0.5/1, delivers the highest specific capacitance of 175 F/g at 0.5 A/g in 1 M KOH. Furthermore, this electrode exhibits exceptional cycling stability, maintaining its initial capacitance after 10,000 charge-discharge cycles, even at a current density of 10 A/g. Overall, the findings highlight the potential of converting hookah tobacco waste into efficient and sustainable electrode materials for high-performance supercapacitors.
title: Green Production of Hookah Tobacco Waste-Derived Porous Carbon and Its Capacitive Performance
